novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanistic relationship—not merely a new setting—by asking whether “distinct, monosemantic, causally-steerable features” separately encode belief attribution and factual assertion, and whether their “entanglement” predicts belief/fact conflation. The closest work I found is “Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact” (behavioral distinction), alongside “Decomposing Theory of Mind: How Emotional Processing Mediates ToM Abilities in LLMs” (2025, linear-probe analysis plus activation steering) and “SAIF: A Sparse Autoencoder Framework for Interpreting and Steering Instruction Following of Language Models” (2025, SAE-based causal steering); I searched combinations including “SAE belief attribution fact knowledge LLM,” “sparse autoencoder epistemic beliefs language model,” “SAE theory of mind belief steering,” and “LLM belief fact distinction mechanistic interpretability.” The step from these works to the claim requires a new core relationship—dictionary-level disentanglement and an entanglement-to-behavior prediction—rather than a direct transfer, although its SAE and steering components are established, supporting a high-but-not-paradigm-level 7.
